h1: Siripanna Villa Resort & Spa — a Lanna resort with a real rice paddy tucked into the middle of Chiang Mai
intro: Picture a resort where you step out of your room and find a real, green rice paddy, old rice barns, Lanna-style timber houses, and big longan trees for shade — all just 10 minutes from the Night Bazaar · Siripanna Villa Resort & Spa is a 5-star Lanna resort in the Wat Gate area that pulls off something remarkable: it conjures up the rural northern countryside right in the middle of the city · It now belongs to the Centara Boutique Collection (SHA Extra Plus) · It scores 8.4 from 178 reviews on Trip.com, with rooms from around ฿2,800/night

The Slee Banyan restaurant, an open-air Lanna setting overlooking the garden
A treatment room at SiriDivana Spa, in warm Lanna-style wood tones

body.html: The first thing that sets Siripanna apart from other Chiang Mai resorts is the real rice paddy growing in the middle of the grounds · It's not a decorative garden or a pretty pond — it's an actual paddy with real green rice plants, and at certain times guests can even try planting or harvesting rice alongside the team · Around it you'll find old rice barns, Lanna-style timber houses, a deck under a big longan tree, and distant mountains as a backdrop — the rural northern countryside recreated inside the city · A lot of guests say the same thing: once you walk through the gate, you can hardly believe you're still only a few minutes from the main tourist district · The resort's aim is to tell the story of Lanna farming life through its architecture and use of space, not just to sell rooms — so even the pathways, the wooden bridges over the canal, and the seating nooks by the paddy are laid out so you can stop and take a photo almost anywhere

The big picture and the backstory: Siripanna Villa Resort & Spa has been open since 2009 and was once talked about as one of the most beautiful Lanna resorts in Chiang Mai in its day, winning a Thailand Boutique Award · It later joined the Centara Boutique Collection and earned SHA Extra Plus certification for safety and hygiene · All along, the resort has positioned itself as a place for families, couples, and seminar groups who want a genuine northern atmosphere at a price that isn't as steep as the luxury resorts · The main selling point isn't lavish materials but the "space" and the "atmosphere" that an ordinary in-town resort simply can't offer — the rice paddy, the wide gardens, and a quiet you rarely find this close to a tourist district

Who it suits: Siripanna is a good fit for anyone who wants the full Lanna mood without driving far out of the city · It works for families who want their kids to see rice paddies, ducks, and local life, for couples after a quiet resort with a spa, and for travelers who still want to walk the night market on the same evening · But if you're after a luxury hotel where everything is brand new and flawless, read the "What real reviews say" section below carefully first — the resort has been open since 2009, and some reviews mention upkeep

Location and getting around: Siripanna sits on Rat Uthit Road in the Wat Gate area, on the east bank of the Ping River · The standout point is that it's only about a 10-minute drive from the Night Bazaar, roughly 12–15 minutes from Tha Phae Gate and the Old City, and about 15–20 minutes from Chiang Mai Airport (CNX) · The Wat Gate area itself is a charming old neighborhood with Wat Ketkaram, riverside cafés, and a morning market to wander · One thing to note: the area around the resort doesn't have a dense cluster of restaurants like Nimman or the Old City, so if you want to head out at night you'll mostly need to call a Grab, which is convenient and cheap

Rooms and decor: The roughly 132 rooms are designed in a Lanna-meets-modern style, with warm wood tones, gabled roofs, and local handcrafted touches · An entry-level room like the S Loft Deluxe runs about 33 sqm, while the Deluxe Lanna is more spacious at over 40 sqm — bigger than the standard rooms at many hotels in the same price range · What reviews praise most often is the soft beds and roomy spaces; many rooms open onto different views — some look out on the rice paddy, some on old rice barns, timber houses, or the pool · Higher categories like the Deluxe Plunge Pool (about 42 sqm) have a private plunge pool off the balcony, and the Royal Lanna Villa is a large villa for those who want full privacy · The rooms come with everything you'd expect at a 5-star resort — minibar, safe, tea/coffee maker, and air conditioning · Most bathrooms have separate wet and dry zones, and some have a bathtub · One thing to know: some of the woodwork and decor pieces have been there since the resort opened — those who like a classic feel will find them charming, but anyone expecting the latest design may feel they're not as up to date as a newly opened boutique hotel

"Opened the curtains in the morning to green rice fields and a duck walking past — felt like staying at a country house upcountry, even though it's really just a ten-minute drive into the city for a bowl of khao soi."

Facilities, pool, and spa: The resort's highlight is the roughly 300 sqm outdoor pool, designed to wind like the Ping River, with a jacuzzi and a shallow area for kids · The pool is shaded by big trees, so it doesn't get too hot even at midday · The SiriDivana Spa is another spot reviews talk about most positively — a calm setting, skilled therapists, and local herbal products · There's also a fitness room, free parking, free Wi-Fi, and a paid shuttle to the airport and into town

Food and bars: The resort's main dining room is Slee Banyan, which serves Thai-Lanna and international dishes in an open-air setting overlooking the garden, plus Nakwan Café for coffee and snacks · The breakfast buffet is praised very often — there's both Thai and Western fare, eggs cooked to order, seasonal fruit, and northern dishes like khao soi or nam ngiao on some days · There's a poolside bar for cold drinks in the afternoon · Many guests say breakfast by the garden is their favorite part of the day — sipping coffee looking out over the green paddy, listening to birdsong, a scene that's hard to find at an in-town resort · One thing to note: because the location is fairly quiet, there aren't many dining options within walking distance, so for dinner many people choose to eat at the resort or grab a Grab into town to the well-known northern restaurants in Wat Gate and along the Ping River nearby · Food prices at the resort are at the usual 5-star level — not as cheap as the places outside, but the quality and atmosphere are worth it

Service: Most guests say the staff are friendly and helpful — warm, happy to call a car for you, and good with kids · This is one reason many people keep coming back even though the building isn't the newest anymore · The team can help arrange local activities, recommend temple and mountain trips, and call a Grab or rental car for you · That said, because the resort also takes seminars and tour groups, the atmosphere can get livelier than expected during big events, so if you really want quiet, it's worth asking when you book whether there's a large group, and choosing a room away from the meeting-room zone

Activities and the surroundings: Because it's in Wat Gate, a charming old neighborhood, there's more to explore around the resort than you'd think · Wat Ketkaram and the Wat Gate community museum are nearby, and the riverside cafés along the Ping and the morning market are just a few minutes' drive · The resort itself runs seasonal activities — rice planting and harvesting, northern cooking, and beginner massage classes — which are great for families who want their kids to try local life · For those who want to venture farther, Doi Suthep, Doi Inthanon, or the various mountain cafés are an easy drive from the resort, since it's on the side that reaches the main roads quickly · You could call it a complete base for exploring Chiang Mai, both the city and the nature side

What real reviews say (both praise and gripes): On the praise side, guests credit the rice-paddy concept and the Lanna atmosphere as something you won't easily find in the city, followed by roomy rooms, soft beds, a good spa, tasty breakfast, and lovely staff · The most common gripe is upkeep — some reviews say certain rooms and spots around the resort are starting to show their age (open since 2009), and some people found the cleanliness of rooms or the pool inconsistent · Another thing many mention is mosquitoes and insects, which is normal for a resort with a rice paddy and lots of greenery — bring your own mosquito repellent · Overall it scores 8.4 from 178 Trip.com reviews, plus around 176 more on Booking.com, reflecting that most people are happy, though some would like the room condition improved

Price comparison and value: Siripanna's starting price is around ฿2,800–฿3,800/night for a Deluxe room in the normal season, climbing during high season (November–February) · Compared with other 5-star Lanna resorts in Chiang Mai like 137 Pillars House or Raya Heritage, which start in the five figures, Siripanna delivers a Lanna atmosphere, generous space, and a real rice paddy at a far more accessible price · The value lies in getting the "rural northern resort experience in the middle of the city" on a modest budget · But compared with newer design hotels in Nimman at a similar price, you're trading brand-new rooms for the charm of the atmosphere and the space · For families traveling together, having room for kids to run around, a big pool, and spacious rooms makes it better value than booking several rooms at a cramped in-town hotel · That said, it's worth checking the promotions on each platform, because sometimes Agoda or Trip.com have deals that include breakfast or a discount that change the nightly rate by several hundred baht

Good to know before booking: One — choose your room type and view carefully; if you want a paddy or garden view, specify it when booking, because some rooms face inward or look onto the parking lot · Two — bring mosquito repellent, and pack comfortable walking shoes since the grounds are large and involve a fair bit of walking · Three — if you want quiet, ask the resort whether there's a large seminar group on your dates · Four — the location relies on Grab for getting into town at night, so budget a little for transport · Five — always compare prices across platforms (Agoda / Booking / Trip.com) before booking, as promotions vary quite a bit by period

The bottom line: Siripanna Villa Resort & Spa is a Lanna resort with "the real thing" to experience — rice paddy, rice barns, timber houses, and a stream that echoes the Ping — in a location that's still only a few minutes' drive into the city · It's a great fit for families and couples who want a genuine northern atmosphere, generous space, a good spa, and a tasty breakfast, on a budget more reachable than the five-figure luxury resorts · You just have to accept that the resort has been open for over a decade, some spots aren't brand new, and there are mosquitoes that come with the rice-paddy setting · If you can live with those two things and value charm over newness, this is one of the most worthwhile and memorable choices in Chiang Mai · For someone who's read a lot of reviews, Siripanna isn't a resort that wins on the precision of its materials or its newness, but on mood and memory — waking up to a green rice paddy, kids playing by the pool, and an unhurried breakfast by the garden are the things guests remember long after they get home · If you're planning a Chiang Mai trip that's a genuine rest mixed with a little city sightseeing, and you want a stay that's a destination in itself, booking ahead in high season and specifying a paddy-view room will get you the best experience here

honestSummary: Siripanna is a resort that sells the charm of "real Lanna" — a real rice paddy, generous space, the rural northern atmosphere in the middle of the city — at a more accessible price than the five-figure luxury resorts · But you have to accept that it's been open for over a decade, some spots aren't brand new, and there are mosquitoes that come with the setting
honestChecks: If you expect a luxury hotel where everything is new and flawless — the resort has been open since 2009 and some rooms are showing their age → consider a newer design hotel in town, or pay more for a ฿10,000+ resort

If you react badly to mosquitoes or worry about insects — the rice paddy and gardens have lots of greenery, so mosquitoes are normal → bring your own repellent, and choose an upper-floor room if you're very concerned

If you want to walk to restaurants/markets from your hotel — Wat Gate is quiet and there aren't many places within walking distance → plan to use Grab into town, or stay in Nimman or the Old City instead

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Siripanna Villa Resort & Spa Chiang Mai

faq.q: Where is Siripanna Villa Resort in Chiang Mai, and how do you get there?
faq.a: Siripanna sits at 36 Rat Uthit Road, in the Wat Gate area on the east bank of the Ping River · It's about a 10-minute drive from the Night Bazaar · 12–15 minutes from the Old City and Tha Phae Gate · around 15–20 minutes from Chiang Mai Airport · The area is quiet, with old temples and riverside cafés to wander; at night it's best to call a Grab into town

faq.q: What's Siripanna's starting price, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around ฿2,800/night for the S Loft Deluxe · The Deluxe Lanna, over 40 sqm, starts at about ฿3,200 · There's a Deluxe Plunge Pool with a private plunge pool, and the Royal Lanna Villa, a large villa for families · Prices depend on the season and package — it's best to compare Agoda / Booking / Trip.com before booking

faq.q: Does the resort have a real rice paddy, and is it good for kids?
faq.a: Yes — there's a real rice paddy growing in the middle of the grounds, along with old rice barns, Lanna timber houses, and big longan trees · It's great for families with kids, since there's room to roam, a big pool with a shallow area, and a countryside setting where children can learn about local life

faq.q: What downsides do real reviews mention?
faq.a: The most common gripe is upkeep — the resort has been open since 2009, so some rooms and spots are showing their age, and there are reviews about inconsistent cleanliness · The other is mosquitoes and insects that come with the rice-paddy setting, so bring repellent · At times there are seminar groups that make it livelier than expected

faq.q: Is Siripanna good value compared with other Lanna resorts?
faq.a: It's good value for anyone who wants a Lanna atmosphere and a real rice paddy on a reachable budget · Compared with 137 Pillars House or Raya Heritage, which start in the five figures, Siripanna starts in the low thousands — but you trade that for rooms that are less new · It suits people who value charm and space over brand-new luxury

faq.q: Which room should you choose, and what should you watch out for when booking?
faq.a: We'd specify a rice-paddy or garden-view room, since some rooms face inward or look onto the parking lot · If you want privacy, go for the Plunge Pool or the Royal Villa · Bring mosquito repellent, and if you want quiet, ask whether there's a large seminar group on your dates
